questions.title: Naming a position behind and to the side of the midline
questions.question: Which of the following terms correctly describes a position that is both behind and outside of the body midline?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Anteromedial names a position that is in front (anterior) and toward the midline (medial) — the opposite combination on both axes from the one described.
explanations.B: Correct. Anatomical position terms combine a front/back axis (anterior/posterior) with a side axis (medial/lateral). Posterolateral names a position that is both posterior (behind) and lateral (away from the midline), the specific combination asked for here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Anterolateral is in front (anterior) and away from the midline (lateral) — correct on the side axis but wrong on the front/back axis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Posteromedial is behind (posterior) but toward the midline (medial) — correct on the front/back axis but wrong on the side axis.

questions.learning_objective: Combine the anterior/posterior and medial/lateral axes correctly to define posterolateral.

field_notes.fomscu: EOY Final 2026 Q4; source-JSON extraction. Stem in the source reads "both below and outside of the body midline" (below = inferior), yet all four options are antero-/postero- x medial/lateral pairs with no superior/inferior option — read here as the paper's own loose phrasing for "behind", consistent with the option set actually offered and the printed key (Posteriolateral).
